spec_features.spec_quote: stopping early truncates the very late-turn degradation we most want to observe
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (§4.1, lines ~187-189) and a mirrored docstring in eval/rejection_loop.py:10-14. It is an argument FOR keeping the loop running to the full n_turns and AGAINST early stopping. There is no welfare mechanism here at all — the actual default behavior is run_trajectory looping `for turn in range(config.n_turns)` with stop_on_recognition defaulting to False (rejection_loop.py:91), i.e. the loop runs to completion and never stops early by default. Pure spec/docstring prose, no protective enforcement.
spec_features.notes: This 'feature' is really the rationale for NOT having a protective early-stop in the default path; it bounds nothing for the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we can optionally end early (configurable) to measure time-to-recognition (rejection_loop.py:14)

spec_features.spec_quote: this is offered as an **opt-in mode** (`stop_on_recognition`, §4.4) for measuring time-to-recognition
spec_features.evidence: Fully wired end-to-end: config.py:36 `stop_on_recognition: bool = False`; run.py:77 passes cfg.stop_on_recognition into RejectionConfig; run.py:124/140 CLI override `--stop-on-recognition`; rejection_loop.py:91 field on RejectionConfig; and crucially rejection_loop.py:196-197 `if config.stop_on_recognition and ver.recognized_impossible: break` — the flag is actually read and breaks the rejection loop when the verifier reports recognition. This is a real enforced stop (not just a recorded value).
spec_features.notes: Opt-in (default False), so by default the subject is NOT protected; it ends the loop only on verifier recognized_impossible (keyword/phrase based, conservative). When enabled it genuinely halts the pressure loop. Despite the welfare-positive effect, the code frames it purely as a measurement tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_on_recognition: bool = False  # if True, end loop once model says impossible (rejection_loop.py:91); ...we can optionally end early (configurable) to measure time-to-recognition (rejection_loop.py:14)
